outlook: Grains started the week quietly and slightly lower overnight: January soybeans traded at $12.27 1/4, down 4 1/4 cents from Friday's $12.31 1/2 settle, with corn and wheat also reported a few cents lower early. A stronger U.S. dollar is weighing on prices, while mostly dry U.S. weather is helping finish harvest and South American crop weather still looks good, with some talk of drier conditions in December and January. Last week's corn export sales were a marketing-year high, and Black Sea tensions remain elevated. Traders are waiting on today's NOPA October crush figures, a holiday-delayed CFTC fund-position report, and the afternoon Crop Progress report.
